title: Minerva identifies nickel-catalyzed Suzuki reaction conditions
summary: Minerva combines Gaussian-process optimization with automated high-throughput experiments to search reaction conditions. In the nickel-catalyzed Suzuki campaign, the preprint reports a condition with 76 area-percent yield and 92% selectivity, while two chemist-designed screening plates did not find successful conditions. Area percent is a chromatographic assay measure, not isolated yield. The preprint and expanded journal report are one study; this does not establish invention of Suzuki coupling or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Minerva Gaussian-process surrogate; Bayesian acquisition; automated HTE

evidence.tested: Experimental 96-well optimization reports 76 AP yield and 92% selectivity; two expert-designed screening plates did not find successful conditions.
evidence.unknown: Product assay area-percent is not isolated yield; pharmaceutical structures and independent replication remain unreviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A GP surrogate and Bayesian acquisition choose batches for automated experiments and use measured outcomes to update condition search.

source_review.scope: Primary ChemRxiv v1 full-text PDF and primary PubMed/journal metadata and abstract checked; journal full PMC direct open CAPTCHA challenged. Exact first-version content for later API case studies is excluded from draft.
